records.source: This paints behind every module screen, on machines that are simultaneously running Cellpose on a GPU and a 40-plate pipeline, so cost is a correctness requirement rather than a nicety. Two things get it there:
records.translation: Detta ritas bakom varje modulskärm, på datorer som samtidigt kör Cellpose på en GPU och en pipeline med 40 plattor, så kostnaden är ett korrekthetskrav snarare än en finess. Två saker gör det möjligt:

records.context: 1. *The timer stops whenever the widget is not on application view* — hidden, on another tab, or in a minimised window. Zero frames, zero CPU. These application views stay open for hours, so this is the whole ball game. 2. *Diffuse themes are painted into a small reusable QImage and scaled up*. The buffer's long edge is whatever the theme declares (:attr:`_BufferedEngine.base_edge`) times the user's resolution setting, so diffuse fields shade ~37 000 pixels instead of ~2 000 000. The aurora and data-art materials preserve native display detail within the actual application view-pixel budget. Aurora returns an owned frame, avoiding a second full-size copy when a shading worker publishes it. 3. *The shading happens on its own independent execution path* (:class:`_FrameProducer`), so the main GUI execution path's whole share of a frame is one ``drawImage``. That is the next section, and it is the one that matters while a workflow is executing.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient#16
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. *The timer stops whenever the widget is not on screen* — hidden, on another tab, or in a minimised window. Zero frames, zero CPU. These screens stay open for hours, so this is the whole ball game. 2. *Diffuse themes are painted into a small reusable QImage and scaled up*. The buffer's long edge is whatever the theme declares (:attr:`_BufferedEngine.base_edge`) times the user's resolution setting, so diffuse fields shade ~37 000 pixels instead of ~2 000 000. The aurora and data-art materials preserve native display detail within the actual screen-pixel budget. Aurora returns an owned frame, avoiding a second full-size copy when a shading worker publishes it. 3. *The shading happens on its own thread* (:class:`_FrameProducer`), so the GUI thread's whole share of a frame is one ``drawImage``. That is the next section, and it is the one that matters while a pipeline is running.
records.translation: 1. *Timern stannar när widgeten inte syns på skärmen* — dold, på en annan flik eller i ett minimerat fönster. Noll bildrutor, noll CPU. Dessa skärmar står öppna i timmar, så detta är helt avgörande. 2. *Diffusa teman ritas i en liten återanvändbar QImage och skalas upp*. Buffertens långa sida är vad temat deklarerar (:attr:`_BufferedEngine.base_edge`) gånger användarens upplösningsinställning, så diffusa fält skuggar ~37 000 pixlar i stället för ~2 000 000. Aurora- och dataartmaterialen behåller skärmens ursprungliga detaljnivå inom den faktiska pixelbudgeten. Aurora returnerar en egen bildruta, vilket undviker en andra kopia i full storlek när en skuggningsarbetare publicerar den. 3. *Skuggningen sker i en egen tråd* (:class:`_FrameProducer`), så GUI-trådens hela andel av en bildruta är en ``drawImage``. Det är nästa avsnitt, och det är det som spelar roll medan en pipeline körs.

records.context: So **CPU saturation is not a cause**: numpy releases the interpreter lock and a core burning flat out costs this module nothing. **A signal flood is not a cause on its own**: 200 lines a second are free, and it only bites in the thousands, where the console's own per-line work saturates the main GUI execution path and nothing in *this* module can help. What is left is **the interpreter lock**: identical drawing work, eleven times slower, because the shading pass is Python and numpy and something else is holding the lock.

records.source: So **CPU saturation is not a cause**: numpy releases the interpreter lock and a core burning flat out costs this module nothing. **A signal flood is not a cause on its own**: 200 lines a second are free, and it only bites in the thousands, where the console's own per-line work saturates the GUI thread and nothing in *this* module can help. What is left is **the interpreter lock**: identical drawing work, eleven times slower, because the shading pass is Python and numpy and something else is holding the lock.
records.translation: Alltså är **CPU-mättnad inte en orsak**: numpy släpper interpretatorlåset och en kärna som går för fullt kostar ingenting för denna modul. **En flod av signaler är inte i sig en orsak**: 200 rader per sekund är gratis, och det märks först vid tusentals, där konsolens eget arbete per rad mättar GUI-tråden och inget i *denna* modul kan hjälpa. Det som återstår är **interpretatorlåset**: identiskt ritarbete, elva gånger långsammare, eftersom skuggningssteget är Python och numpy och något annat håller låset.

records.context: In that historical ``blobs`` benchmark, the rate goes from 17.3 fps to 24.7 on the same worker. Two levers finish the job and neither is in this file — ``sys.setswitchinterval(0.001)`` in the Qt bootstrap (measured independently: 32 % of the frame rate to 99 %, for about 6 % of the worker's throughput) and coalescing ``PipelineWorker.line_ready``.

records.context: Three constraints shape the implementation. Animation periods are sampled from continuous ranges rather than replayed from a precomputed loop, avoiding visible jumps and large frame caches. Shading runs outside the main GUI execution path; if a frame is late, the previous frame is repeated and counted by :attr:`AmbientWidget.repeated_frames`. The animation clock remains on the main GUI execution path, and rendered frames remain deterministic functions of ``(seed, clock, size)``.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient#56
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Three constraints shape the implementation. Animation periods are sampled from continuous ranges rather than replayed from a precomputed loop, avoiding visible jumps and large frame caches. Shading runs outside the GUI thread; if a frame is late, the previous frame is repeated and counted by :attr:`AmbientWidget.repeated_frames`. The animation clock remains on the GUI thread, and rendered frames remain deterministic functions of ``(seed, clock, size)``.
records.translation: Tre begränsningar formar implementationen. Animationsperioder samplas från kontinuerliga intervall i stället för att spelas upp från en förberäknad slinga, vilket undviker synliga hopp och stora bildrutecacher. Skuggningen körs utanför GUI-tråden; om en bildruta är sen upprepas den föregående och räknas av :attr:`AmbientWidget.repeated_frames`. Animationsklockan stannar i GUI-tråden, och renderade bildrutor förblir deterministiska funktioner av ``(seed, clock, size)``.

records.context: An engine owns no widget and no timer. It holds the constants rolled once from its seed, a clock (:attr:`time`), and whatever reusable buffer it paints through. Everything it draws is a pure function of ``(seed, time, width, height, colours, background)`` — which is what lets a test render the same frame twice and compare it byte for byte, and what lets :meth:`AmbientWidget.set_theme` swap engines without the animation jumping.

records.source: An engine owns no widget and no timer. It holds the constants rolled once from its seed, a clock (:attr:`time`), and whatever reusable buffer it paints through. Everything it draws is a pure function of ``(seed, time, width, height, colours, background)`` — which is what lets a test render the same frame twice and compare it byte for byte, and what lets :meth:`AmbientWidget.set_theme` swap engines without the animation jumping.
records.translation: En motor äger ingen widget och ingen timer. Den håller de konstanter som slumpats en gång från dess frö, en klocka (:attr:`time`) och den återanvändbara buffert den ritar genom. records.context: Additive compositing means N overlapping shapes are N times the light, so a density control with no compensation is a *brightness* control wearing a misleading name. Measured, on a page at 0.076: mean frame lightness went from 0.135 at density 1.0 to 0.288 at 3.0. The backdrop would have become the loudest thing behind a settings form — which the alphas in this module were set on a rendered frame specifically to prevent (see :data:`AURORA_ALPHA_DARK`).
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.AmbientEngine.alpha_scale#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Additive compositing means N overlapping shapes are N times the light, so a density control with no compensation is a *brightness* control wearing a misleading name. Measured, on a page at 0.076: mean frame lightness went from 0.135 at density 1.0 to 0.288 at 3.0. The backdrop would have become the loudest thing behind a settings form — which the alphas in this module were set on a rendered frame specifically to prevent (see :data:`AURORA_ALPHA_DARK`).
records.translation: Additiv sammansättning innebär att N överlappande former ger N gånger ljuset, så en täthetskontroll utan kompensation är en *ljusstyrkekontroll* med ett missvisande namn. Uppmätt på en sida med 0.076: bildrutans medelljushet gick från 0.135 vid täthet 1.0 till 0.288 vid 3.0. Bakgrunden skulle ha blivit det mest framträdande bakom ett inställningsformulär — vilket alfavärdena i denna modul ställdes in på en renderad bildruta just för att förhindra (se :data:`AURORA_ALPHA_DARK`).

records.context: So above 1.0 the field's light is *divided among* more elements rather than added to it. Below 1.0 nothing is done: quadrupling the alpha of a quarter as many blobs clips to white rather than compensating, and a sparser field being a quieter one is the right answer anyway.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.AmbientEngine.alpha_scale#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So above 1.0 the field's light is *divided among* more elements rather than added to it. Below 1.0 nothing is done: quadrupling the alpha of a quarter as many blobs clips to white rather than compensating, and a sparser field being a quieter one is the right answer anyway.
records.translation: Över 1.0 *fördelas* därför fältets ljus mellan fler element i stället för att adderas. Under 1.0 görs ingenting: att fyrdubbla alfa för en fjärdedel så många klumpar klipps till vitt i stället för att kompensera, och att ett glesare fält är ett stillsammare är ändå rätt svar.

records.context: Density therefore changes the *texture* of the field — how many shapes it is made of, and how strongly each one states itself — and not how loud the field is. That is the only reading of the control that leaves the backdrop legible at both ends of its range.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.AmbientEngine.alpha_scale#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Density therefore changes the *texture* of the field — how many shapes it is made of, and how strongly each one states itself — and not how loud the field is. That is the only reading of the control that leaves the backdrop legible at both ends of its range.
records.translation: Tätheten ändrar därför fältets *textur* — hur många former det består av och hur tydligt var och en framträder — och inte hur intensivt fältet är. Det är den enda tolkningen av kontrollen som håller bakgrunden läsbar i båda ändarna av intervallet.

records.context: The one exception is a backdrop that stops while it is still on application view -- a CPU-heavy run pausing the animation (:func:`_animation_paused_for_work`), reduced motion, or the animation switched off. records.context: :meth:`geometry` yields ``(x, y_bottom, visible_height, brightness)`` per sampled column of every curtain, in pixels, ``AURORA_COLUMNS + 1`` of them per curtain in curtain order. The painter builds its paths from exactly those numbers, so a test that tracks a fold crest through ``geometry`` is tracking the crest that is on application view. ``brightness`` is the travelling surge. Seeded irregular ray positions and independent continuous length and brightness cycles modulate the sampled sheet, with tapered tops. Roll the aurora's bands and their drift.

records.source: :meth:`geometry` yields ``(x, y_bottom, visible_height, brightness)`` per sampled column of every curtain, in pixels, ``AURORA_COLUMNS + 1`` of them per curtain in curtain order. The painter builds its paths from exactly those numbers, so a test that tracks a fold crest through ``geometry`` is tracking the crest that is on screen. ``brightness`` is the travelling surge. Seeded irregular ray positions and independent continuous length and brightness cycles modulate the sampled sheet, with tapered tops. Roll the aurora's bands and their drift.
records.translation: :meth:`geometry` ger ``(x, y_bottom, visible_height, brightness)`` per samplad kolumn i varje draperi, i pixlar, ``AURORA_COLUMNS + 1`` per draperi i draperiordning. Slumpade oregelbundna strålpositioner och oberoende kontinuerliga längd- och ljusstyrkecykler modulerar det samplade skiktet, med avsmalnande toppar. Slumpar aurorans band och deras drift.

records.context: Always built from the palette's *first* colour, wandering up to :data:`AURORA_HUE_BLEND` of the way towards one of the others and back. Every curtain shares that body colour on purpose: the body of an aurora is a single emission line — 557.7 nm oxygen — and the palette's remaining entries are the top and the fringe, which the ramp puts above and below it. Giving curtain two a red body and curtain three a violet one, which is what indexing the palette by curtain would do, is the one thing that stops the whole theme reading as an aurora.

records.source: The compensation on the base class exists because overlapping translucent *fields* pile up additively. A starfield does not have that problem — measured, its mean frame lightness moves from 0.076 to 0.077 across the whole density range, because a couple of hundred dots light 0.65 % of the page and almost never land on each other. Dividing their alpha by three would not un-brighten anything; it would hide two thirds of the stars in the background.
records.translation: Kompensationen i basklassen finns eftersom överlappande genomskinliga *fält* adderas. records.context: The profile is the default for one reason that outweighs its cost: **the Wald interval is finite by construction.** It is ``L ± t·SE``, so it returns a finite, symmetric interval even for a curve whose midpoint the data does not locate at all. The profile interval can *fail to close*: the residual sum of squares stays under the threshold all the way out to a concentration ten thousand times the highest dose tested, and that failure is the diagnostic. It is reported as an open bound, not smoothed into a number.

records.context: It is nonetheless **not the default**. The fifth parameter trades off against the Hill slope — many (slope, asymmetry) pairs draw nearly the same curve — so on the eight or ten concentrations a plate actually carries it is weakly identified, and the profile interval it produces is correspondingly wider. The module therefore offers it, fits it **from the 4PL solution** so the asymmetric search starts at the symmetric answer, and reports an extra-sum-of-squares F test of the one added parameter in :attr:`DoseResponseResult.asymmetry_p` so a reader can see whether the asymmetry was worth what it cost.

Den femte parametern konkurrerar med Hill-lutningen — många par av (lutning, asymmetri) ritar nästan samma kurva — så med de åtta eller tio koncentrationer som en platta faktiskt har är den svagt identifierad, och det profilintervall den ger blir motsvarande bredare. Modulen erbjuder den därför, anpassar den **från 4PL-lösningen** så att den asymmetriska sökningen startar i det symmetriska svaret, och rapporterar ett F-test med extra kvadratsumma för den enda tillagda parametern i :attr:`DoseResponseResult.asymmetry_p`, så att läsaren kan se om asymmetrin var värd sin kostnad.

Sådana anpassningar redovisar fyndet i :attr:`DoseResponseResult.hormesis` och i sina förbehåll.

records.translation: Varje resultat innehåller residualstandardfelet, R² och — när designen har replikat — ett **F-test för bristande anpassning mot rent fel**. Det sista testar om kurvformen passar datat, vilket R² inte gör.

records.context: R² on a sigmoid is nearly uninformative. Any monotone curve through a microplate sample position-sampled dose–response scores above 0.95, because the total sum of squares is dominated by the difference between the two plateaus and *any* S-shaped line captures that. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` says so next to the number, every time.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#36
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: R² on a sigmoid is nearly uninformative. Any monotone curve through a well-sampled dose–response scores above 0.95, because the total sum of squares is dominated by the difference between the two plateaus and *any* S-shaped line captures that. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` says so next to the number, every time.
records.translation: R² för en sigmoid säger nästan ingenting. Varje monoton kurva genom en välsamplad dos–respons får över 0.95, eftersom den totala kvadratsumman domineras av skillnaden mellan de två platåerna och *vilken* S-formad linje som helst fångar den. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` anger detta bredvid talet, varje gång.

records.context: The lack-of-fit test does the real work when replicates exist: pure error (within-concentration scatter, ``n - m`` df) is a model-free estimate of noise, and the residual variance in excess of it (``m - 4`` df) is model-misspecification. A small p-value means a 4PL is the wrong shape for this data whatever the R² says. With no replicates there is no pure-error estimate and the test does not exist — which is itself reported, because "cannot be tested" and "passed" are different states.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#37
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The lack-of-fit test does the real work when replicates exist: pure error (within-concentration scatter, ``n - m`` df) is a model-free estimate of noise, and the residual variance in excess of it (``m - 4`` df) is model-misspecification. A small p-value means a 4PL is the wrong shape for this data whatever the R² says. With no replicates there is no pure-error estimate and the test does not exist — which is itself reported, because "cannot be tested" and "passed" are different states.
records.translation: Testet för bristande anpassning gör det verkliga arbetet när replikat finns: rent fel (spridning inom koncentrationer, ``n - m`` df) är en modellfri skattning av bruset, och residualvariansen utöver det (``m - 4`` df) är felspecifikation av modellen. Ett litet p-värde betyder att en 4PL har fel form för detta data, vad R² än säger. Utan replikat finns ingen skattning av rent fel och testet existerar inte — vilket i sig rapporteras, eftersom "cannot be tested" (kan inte testas) och "passed" (godkänt) är olika tillstånd.

records.context: **The doses are geometric.** A 2- or 3-fold dilution series is evenly spaced in log concentration and violently uneven in linear concentration. The information the experiment carries about the midpoint is information about *which dilution step* it sits on, which is a statement in log space.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The doses are geometric.** A 2- or 3-fold dilution series is evenly spaced in log concentration and violently uneven in linear concentration. The information the experiment carries about the midpoint is information about *which dilution step* it sits on, which is a statement in log space.
records.translation: **Doserna är geometriska.** En 2- eller 3-faldig spädningsserie är jämnt fördelad i logaritmisk koncentration och kraftigt ojämn i linjär koncentration. Den information som experimentet bär om mittpunkten är information om *vilket spädningssteg* den ligger på, vilket är ett påstående i logaritmiskt rum.

records.context: **The likelihood surface is close to symmetric in log10(EC50) and badly skewed in EC50.** That is what makes a quadratic (Wald) approximation defensible on ``log10_ec50`` and indefensible on ``EC50``.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.translation: **Likelihoodytan är nära symmetrisk i log10(EC50) och kraftigt skev i EC50.** Det är det som gör en kvadratisk (Wald) approximation försvarbar för ``log10_ec50`` och oförsvarbar för ``EC50``.

records.context: **A linear-space interval routinely reaches below zero**, and a negative concentration is impossible: an EC50 of ``1.0 ± 1.4 µM`` is an interval that includes impossible values.

records.context: Reporting therefore back-transforms the *interval*: ``10 ** [lo, hi]``. The result is multiplicative (``0.62 – 1.61 µM`` around 1.0, a 1.6-fold factor either way), always positive, and multiplicative like potency itself.

records.context: Pooling is two-stage. Each plate is fitted on its own -- by the same :func:`fit_dose_response` that fits everything else, with the same refusals -- and the per-plate log10 EC50s are then combined with a random-effects weight. One joint nonlinear mixed model would be the other way to do it; it would also mean a second fitting path with a second set of failure modes, and a plate that :func:`fit_dose_response` refuses would have to be refused again, differently, inside it. This way a refusal on one plate is the same refusal :func:`fit_dose_response` reports.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response.PooledFit#2

records.source: Pooling is two-stage. Each plate is fitted on its own -- by the same :func:`fit_dose_response` that fits everything else, with the same refusals -- and the per-plate log10 EC50s are then combined with a random-effects weight. One joint nonlinear mixed model would be the other way to do it; it would also mean a second fitting path with a second set of failure modes, and a plate that :func:`fit_dose_response` refuses would have to be refused again, differently, inside it. This way a refusal on one plate is the same refusal :func:`fit_dose_response` reports.
records.translation: Sammanslagningen sker i två steg. Varje platta anpassas för sig -- med samma :func:`fit_dose_response` som anpassar allt annat, med samma avslag -- och de log10 EC50s per platta kombineras sedan med en vikt för slumpeffekter. En gemensam icke-linjär blandad modell vore det andra sättet; det skulle också innebära en andra anpassningsväg med en andra uppsättning felfall, och en platta som :func:`fit_dose_response` avvisar skulle behöva avvisas igen, på ett annat sätt, inuti den. På detta sätt är ett avslag för en platta samma avslag som :func:`fit_dose_response` rapporterar.

records.context: The pooling uses random rather than fixed effects. Fixed-effect pooling assumes every plate measures the same value and differs only by noise. Three tight plates that disagree then give a narrow interval around a value none of them support. The DerSimonian-Laird estimate of the between-plate variance is added to each plate's own, so real variation between plates widens the answer instead of being weighted away.

The short version: zeros are vehicle controls and are reported rather than logged; a series that is not monotone is refused rather than fitted; the fit is canonicalised so the Hill slope carries the direction; the EC50 is reported only when the experiment actually locates it, and otherwise as a one-sided bound with :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50` set to ``None``.
records.translation: Hela policyn finns i modulens docstring. Kortversionen: nollor är vehikelkontroller och rapporteras i stället för att logaritmeras; en serie som inte är monoton avvisas i stället för att anpassas; anpassningen kanoniseras så att Hill-lutningen bär riktningen; EC50 rapporteras bara när experimentet faktiskt lokaliserar det, och annars som en ensidig gräns med :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50` satt till ``None``.

records.source: The y axis is the raw P value and is continuous. The reason follows.

records.context: Benjamini-Hochberg's adjusted P is a cumulative minimum taken from the largest P downwards -- ``q_(i) = min over j >= i of (n * p_(j) / j)`` -- and the ``min`` is both what enforces monotonicity and what creates ties: the moment a later rank produces a smaller value, every earlier rank is pulled down onto it. Measured on reference runs: 823 q values with 31 distinct, 19 tied levels covering 811 coefficients, GRA14 and 225160 both at 4.1150e-03. A volcano drawn against that has a staircase for a y-axis, and no transform can separate two tests that hold the same number.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.fast_plots.VolcanoPlot#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Benjamini-Hochberg's adjusted P is a cumulative minimum taken from the largest P downwards -- ``q_(i) = min over j >= i of (n * p_(j) / j)`` -- and the ``min`` is both what enforces monotonicity and what creates ties: the moment a later rank produces a smaller value, every earlier rank is pulled down onto it. Measured on reference runs: 823 q values with 31 distinct, 19 tied levels covering 811 coefficients, GRA14 and 225160 both at 4.1150e-03. A volcano drawn against that has a staircase for a y-axis, and no transform can separate two tests that hold the same number.
records.translation: Benjamini-Hochbergs justerade P är ett kumulativt minimum som tas från det största P nedåt -- ``q_(i) = min over j >= i of (n * p_(j) / j)`` -- och ``min`` är både det som säkerställer monotonicitet och det som skapar lika värden: så snart en senare rang ger ett mindre värde dras varje tidigare rang ner till det. Uppmätt på referenskörningar: 823 q-värden varav 31 distinkta, 19 lika nivåer som täcker 811 koefficienter, GRA14 och 225160 båda vid 4.1150e-03. Ett volcano-diagram som ritas mot detta får en trappa som y-axel, och ingen transform kan skilja två test som har samma tal.

records.context: Point-in-polygon uses the vectorised even–odd ray-casting rule. A row whose x or y is missing is **outside every gate**. Its state is not "unknown", and it is not silently kept. An object with no measurement is not inside the region. Letting it through would put objects with no value into a population the user defined by value; the same rule :class:`~spacr.selection.RangeFilter` applies to NaN.

records.source: Point-in-polygon is the even–odd ray-casting rule, vectorised. A row whose x or y is missing is **outside every gate** — not "unknown", not silently kept. An object with no measurement is not an object inside the region, and letting it through would put objects with no value into a population the user defined by value; the same rule :class:`~spacr.selection.RangeFilter` applies to NaN.
records.translation: Punkt-i-polygon är den jämn–udda strålkastningsregeln, vektoriserad. En rad vars x eller y saknas ligger **utanför varje gate** — inte "unknown" (okänd), inte i tysthet behållen. Ett objekt utan mätning är inte ett objekt inuti regionen, och att släppa igenom det skulle placera objekt utan värde i en population som användaren definierade utifrån värde; samma regel som :class:`~spacr.selection.RangeFilter` tillämpar på NaN.

Without it a single chain of objects bridging two populations merges them, which on a real scatter happens more often than not.
records.translation: ``tolerance`` hur långt från varandra två objekt kan ligga och ändå räknas som grannar. Det är detta som gör den till en VATTENDELARE snarare än en cirkel -- markeringen flödar längs en tät ås och stannar vid ett glapp, så att en avlång eller böjd population kommer med i sin helhet medan det glesa området runt den inte gör det. ``max_radius`` hur långt från KLICKET markeringen över huvud taget får nå. Utan den slår en enda kedja av objekt som förbinder två populationer ihop dem, vilket i ett verkligt spridningsdiagram händer oftare än inte.

records.source: This panel renders :mod:`spacr.measurement_scan` beside regression runs. Model settings remain fixed while the dependent measurement changes. Each row shows both the within-measurement q-value and the correction across all scanned measurements; verdicts use the across-scan value, while ranking uses effect size. In the recorded permuted-label check, within-measurement correction flagged 83.5% of scans and across-scan correction flagged 5.0%.
records.translation: Denna panel renderar :mod:`spacr.measurement_scan` bredvid regressionskörningar. Modellinställningarna förblir fasta medan det beroende mätvärdet ändras. Varje rad visar både q-värdet inom mätvärdet och korrektionen över alla skannade mätvärden; utlåtanden använder värdet över hela skanningen, medan rangordningen använder effektstorleken. I den registrerade kontrollen med permuterade etiketter flaggade korrektion inom mätvärdet 83.5% av skanningarna och korrektion över hela skanningen 5.0%.

records.context: :class:`DatabaseMergePanel` also exposes the measurement databases attached to each regression laboratory microplate. :mod:`spacr.multi_database` prevents pooling colliding laboratory microplate identities, and :mod:`spacr.merge_tables` chooses aggregation and join behavior per table from measurement type and object cardinality. The panel reports the selected sources, dropped columns, aggregation policy, collisions, and other merge consequences rather than applying one global join rule.

records.context: Asked of :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` rather than of ``os.path``. This property is read once per laboratory microplate row by `_fill_table`, and again by `paths`, `screens` and `describe` -- so a project with eight laboratory microplates on a sleeping `autofs` mount was eight twenty-second stats on the main GUI execution path before the tab had drawn anything. The probe answers from a cache, reports a path it has not seen as present, and stats it on its own bounded worker; `DatabaseMergePanel._follow_path_probes` is the half that corrects the row when the real answer lands.

records.source: Asked of :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` rather than of ``os.path``. This property is read once per plate row by `_fill_table`, and again by `paths`, `screens` and `describe` -- so a project with eight plates on a sleeping `autofs` mount was eight twenty-second stats on the GUI thread before the tab had drawn anything. The probe answers from a cache, reports a path it has not seen as present, and stats it on its own bounded worker; `DatabaseMergePanel._follow_path_probes` is the half that corrects the row when the real answer lands.
records.translation: Frågar :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` snarare än ``os.path``. Denna egenskap läses en gång per plattrad av `_fill_table`, och igen av `paths`, `screens` och `describe` -- så ett projekt med åtta plattor på en vilande `autofs`-montering innebar åtta stat-anrop på tjugo sekunder vardera i GUI-tråden innan fliken hade ritat något. Sonden svarar från en cache, rapporterar en sökväg den inte har sett som närvarande och gör stat på den i sin egen begränsade arbetare; `DatabaseMergePanel._follow_path_probes` är den halva som korrigerar raden när det verkliga svaret kommer.

records.context: This composes the two existing merges and adds nothing else. :func:`spacr.multi_database.read_merged` is *many databases, one table*; :func:`spacr.merge_tables.merge_tables` is *one database, many tables* and takes a path, so it cannot be handed a frame that already spans databases. This runs the first per chosen table and then joins them with the second's own :func:`~spacr.merge_tables.roll_up` and :meth:`~spacr.merge_tables.MergePolicy.how_for`. There is no sum and no mean written here; every number comes from the rules.

records.source: This composes the two existing merges and adds nothing else. :func:`spacr.multi_database.read_merged` is *many databases, one table*; :func:`spacr.merge_tables.merge_tables` is *one database, many tables* and takes a path, so it cannot be handed a frame that already spans databases. This runs the first per chosen table and then joins them with the second's own :func:`~spacr.merge_tables.roll_up` and :meth:`~spacr.merge_tables.MergePolicy.how_for`. There is no sum and no mean written here; every number comes from the rules.
records.translation: Detta kombinerar de två befintliga sammanslagningarna och lägger inte till något annat. :func:`spacr.multi_database.read_merged` är *många databaser, en tabell*; :func:`spacr.merge_tables.merge_tables` är *en databas, många tabeller* och tar en sökväg, så den kan inte få en tabell som redan spänner över databaser. Detta kör den första per vald tabell och kopplar sedan ihop dem med den andras egna :func:`~spacr.merge_tables.roll_up` och :meth:`~spacr.merge_tables.MergePolicy.how_for`. Ingen summa och inget medelvärde skrivs här; varje tal kommer från reglerna.

records.context: Nothing in this process parses it back. The frame is already in this process when it is written, and the fits run in this process too, so :func:`spacr.frame_handoff.stage` offers it under the path it wrote before the write returns. A four-plate screen merges to about 2.75 GB: the CSV write cost around 160 seconds before anything read it, and each fit then parsed the whole file back out of the page cache -- minutes of CPU with no disk I/O at all, which is what made a working run look hung.

records.source: Nothing in this process parses it back. The frame is already in this process when it is written, and the fits run in this process too, so :func:`spacr.frame_handoff.stage` offers it under the path it wrote before the write returns. A four-plate screen merges to about 2.75 GB: the CSV write cost around 160 seconds before anything read it, and each fit then parsed the whole file back out of the page cache -- minutes of CPU with no disk I/O at all, which is what made a working run look hung.
records.translation: Inget i denna process tolkar den tillbaka. Tabellen finns redan i processen när den skrivs, och anpassningarna körs också i processen, så :func:`spacr.frame_handoff.stage` erbjuder den under den sökväg den skrev innan skrivningen returnerar. En skärmning med fyra plattor slås samman till ungefär 2.75 GB: skrivningen av CSV kostade omkring 160 sekunder innan något läste den, och varje anpassning tolkade sedan hela filen på nytt ur sidcachen -- minuter av CPU utan någon disk-I/O alls, vilket fick en fungerande körning att se ut att ha hängt sig.

records.source: The offer is a weak reference, so it cannot keep a multi-gigabyte frame alive after the panel that merged it lets go, and a reader that was offered nothing reads the file exactly as before.
